records.practice: Do not infer zero provider retention from no application database or no training. Bedrock retention depends on model, API, region and account/project settings. For Runtime, verify regional account mode none; unknown/denied reads fail closed. Account-wide changes can affect existing workloads and require authorization. Read-only checks are not a model-quality or deployment test.

records.practice: A composed internal application must implement the API and browser alongside hosting: verify the Entra token signature, issuer/tenant, API audience, authorized browser client, delegated scope and assigned user role; never trust caller-provided identity headers. Use managed workload identity and account-scoped model permissions. Package real source with locked dependencies and exact build/image inputs. Keep authorization outside model text and validate output fields before returning them.
limitations: Local RSA/ASGI and scripted model/policy transport tests, plus native AzureRM/AzureAD schemas and mock plans; no deployed identity or model behavior proven.
JWT roles remain usable until token expiry; no continuous revocation or tenant MFA policy is established.

Account data handling requires approved ContentLogging=false before inference. Image startup/scan, real Entra flow, managed-identity exchange, model quality, region availability and authorized account plan remain pending.
Existing company group and RBAC-mode ACR are destination prerequisites; private networks, persistence, tenancy and workflows require more capabilities.

records.practice: Use Cloud Run IAP and company-group access as the browser authorization boundary; independently verify the ES256 signed IAP header, fixed key origin, issuer, exact service audience and bounded lifetime. Unsigned identity headers or a caller bearer header do not establish IAP access. Separate keyless runtime and image-pulling identities; allow only required model/policy reads. Keep model output behind strict schema checks and human review.
limitations: Real local ES256/ASGI tests and scripted transport checks, native Google/Google-beta schemas and mock plans; no live IAP, model or destination proof.
IAP session/group policy and signed-header expiry are distinct from continuous directory revocation or verified MFA.

No app persistence does not prove provider zero retention. Destination-owner abuse-policy review is attested; caching/logging/sharing controls are separately read at runtime. No fabricated approval API or project-wide policy write.

Requires an organization-owned project, existing group and registry, reviewed regional model, built/tested image and account inputs. Image startup/scan, account plans, durable state and workflows remain pending.

records.practice: Separate user authorization from workload authentication. Use the reviewed ContainerAuthenticator with the fixed Code Engine token path and dedicated trusted profile; never embed an application API key. Scope service grants to the reviewed runtime instance and separately verify watsonx project access. Package runnable source and complete hash-locked dependencies. Isolate provider SDK closures that conflict rather than weakening their requirements.
limitations: 15 local cryptographic/HTTP/SDK/scripted checks and Linux/schema/mock evidence; no live identity, model-quality or deployment proof.
New owned App ID tenant only; no existing SSO, MFA, immediate JWT revocation or global logout.
Instance-scoped Writer is broader than inference; project membership is separate. Policy review is operator attestation, not a provider approval API.
Verify existing project/registry/pull secret, regional model/plan/quotas/costs. Persistence and workflows need further implementation.
